title: Preparing a rabbit home
steps: Choose a large, secure living area with room to run, stretch and stand upright.
Provide hay, water, a hiding place, a litter tray and non-slip flooring.
caution: Small hutches alone do not provide enough space for a rabbit's daily needs.

title: Why rabbits need companions
steps: Plan for a compatible rabbit companion, usually a neutered pair.
Introduce rabbits gradually in neutral space and monitor body language.
caution: Never put unfamiliar rabbits together without a careful bonding plan.

title: Rabbit-proofing cables and furniture
steps: Cover electrical cables and block access to hazardous gaps.
Provide safe chew items and supervise access to new rooms.
caution: Chewed electrical cables can cause serious injury.

title: Settling a new rabbit
steps: Keep a consistent routine and allow quiet hiding places.
Sit nearby and let the rabbit approach on its own terms.
caution: Avoid chasing or repeatedly picking up a frightened rabbit.

title: Choosing a rabbit-savvy vet
steps: Find a veterinary practice experienced with rabbits before an emergency.
Ask about vaccinations, neutering and out-of-hours care.
caution: Rabbits can deteriorate quickly when unwell.

title: Unlimited grass hay
steps: Offer clean, fresh grass hay at all times and top it up daily.
Place hay near litter areas to encourage natural grazing.
caution: Hay is essential for gut movement and dental wear; sudden loss of appetite is urgent.

title: Fresh leafy greens
steps: Offer a variety of suitable leafy greens in appropriate amounts.
Introduce new greens slowly and watch droppings and appetite.
caution: Avoid abrupt diet changes; ask a vet about diets for young or ill rabbits.

title: Measuring rabbit pellets
steps: Use a measured portion of plain, high-fibre rabbit pellets appropriate to age and size.
Follow veterinary advice and the manufacturer's feeding guidance.
caution: Muesli-style mixes can encourage selective feeding.

title: Fresh drinking water
steps: Supply clean water in a sturdy bowl and check it several times daily.
Clean the bowl and confirm it has not been tipped over.
caution: A rabbit that is not drinking or eating normally needs prompt veterinary advice.

title: Treats and fruit
steps: Use tiny portions of suitable fruit as occasional treats.
Prefer hay-based enrichment and herbs rather than sugary snacks.
caution: Avoid chocolate, sweets and processed human snacks.

title: Plants and foods to avoid
steps: Identify all plants accessible in the home and garden.
Remove potentially poisonous plants and unknown cuttings.
caution: Contact a vet urgently if you suspect poisoning; do not attempt home remedies.

title: Changing food gradually
steps: Mix small amounts of a new appropriate food into the usual diet over several days.
Monitor appetite, droppings and comfort throughout.
caution: Stop and contact a vet if appetite or droppings reduce.

title: Indoor rabbit exercise area
steps: Provide a roomy exercise area with hiding places and tunnels.
Add traction on smooth floors using washable non-slip mats.
caution: Avoid slippery floors and unstable climbing equipment.

title: Outdoor enclosure security
steps: Use a predator-resistant run with secure mesh and locks.
Provide weatherproof shelter, shade and protection from digging predators.
caution: Check security daily; thin chicken wire alone may not stop predators.

title: Temperature and heat safety
steps: Provide shade, airflow and several cool resting spots in warm weather.
Offer cool ceramic tiles or wrapped cool packs with space to move away.
caution: Heatstroke is an emergency; contact a vet immediately if suspected.

title: Cold and wet weather
steps: Keep bedding dry and provide sheltered, draught-free sleeping spaces.
Check outdoor accommodation after rain, wind and freezing weather.
caution: Avoid sudden temperature changes when moving rabbits indoors and outdoors.

title: Safe bedding choices
steps: Choose clean, low-dust bedding and soft resting surfaces.
Replace damp bedding promptly and monitor for sore feet.
caution: Avoid strongly scented or dusty materials that irritate airways.

title: Cleaning the rabbit enclosure
steps: Remove wet litter and soiled bedding daily.
Clean bowls and surfaces with rabbit-safe products and rinse thoroughly.
caution: Keep rabbits away from cleaning chemicals until areas are dry.

title: Setting up a litter tray
steps: Use a large tray with safe paper-based litter and hay nearby.
Move stray droppings into the tray and reward calm use.
caution: Avoid clumping cat litter and punishment.

title: Preventing sore hocks
steps: Provide clean, dry, soft surfaces and avoid wire flooring.
Check heels regularly for hair loss, redness or sores.
caution: Seek veterinary advice promptly for painful or open lesions.

title: Recognising relaxed body language
steps: Watch for loose posture, normal grooming and comfortable resting.
Notice how your own rabbit signals contentment and curiosity.
caution: A hunched, withdrawn rabbit may be ill rather than simply quiet.

title: Recognising fear and stress
steps: Look for freezing, hiding, thumping or repeated escape attempts.
Reduce noise and allow access to a secure hiding place.
caution: Persistent stress or sudden behaviour change warrants a welfare review.

title: Safe digging activities
steps: Offer a deep box of shredded paper or other rabbit-safe digging material.
Hide a little hay inside to encourage exploration.
caution: Check materials for staples, strings and swallowing hazards.

title: Chewing and foraging toys
steps: Offer untreated rabbit-safe willow, cardboard tubes and hay-filled toys.
Rotate items and scatter-feed part of the usual ration.
caution: Remove toys if pieces become sharp or unsafe to swallow.

title: Gentle trust building
steps: Sit at floor level and let the rabbit come to you.
Offer a little suitable food from your hand without grabbing.
caution: Respect rabbits that dislike being touched or lifted.

title: Safe handling when necessary
steps: Support the chest and hindquarters securely and keep the rabbit close to your body.
Use floor-level handling where possible and ask a vet to demonstrate.
caution: Never lift by ears or scruff; struggling rabbits can injure their spine.

title: Introducing two rabbits
steps: Arrange a health check and neutering plan before bonding.
Use neutral territory, supervised sessions and positive signs such as relaxed proximity.
caution: Separate safely if fighting occurs and seek experienced bonding advice.

title: Enrichment for rainy days
steps: Set up tunnels, hideaways and foraging activities in a sheltered area.
Change the arrangement occasionally without removing familiar safe spaces.
caution: Ensure enough space for both rabbits to move away from each other.

title: Brushing short-haired rabbits
steps: Brush gently according to coat needs, especially during moulting.
Check for mats and skin changes while grooming.
caution: Do not pull out tightly matted fur or cut close to skin.

title: Long-haired rabbit coat care
steps: Check the coat daily for tangles and trapped debris.
Use gentle grooming and ask a rabbit-experienced groomer or vet for help.
caution: Severe matting can damage skin and needs professional attention.

title: Checking nails
steps: Inspect nails regularly for overgrowth and snagging.
Ask a vet or trained professional to demonstrate safe trimming.
caution: The quick can bleed if cut; do not trim if you cannot see safely.

title: Keeping the rear end clean
steps: Inspect the rear end daily for stuck droppings and damp fur.
Address diet, mobility or toileting problems with a vet.
caution: Flystrike can be fatal and requires immediate veterinary care.

title: Why routine bathing is unsuitable
steps: Use gentle spot cleaning only when necessary and veterinary approved.
Keep the rabbit warm and dry after any essential cleaning.
caution: Do not immerse a rabbit in water or use human shampoos.

title: Watching appetite and droppings
steps: Notice normal eating, drinking and droppings every day.
Record any sudden change and contact a rabbit-savvy vet immediately.
caution: Not eating or passing droppings can signal gut stasis and is an emergency.

title: Recognising possible gut stasis
steps: Watch for refusal of food, fewer droppings, hunching or teeth grinding.
Contact an emergency rabbit-savvy vet without delay.
caution: Do not force-feed or give medications without veterinary direction, especially if blockage is possible.

title: Checking rabbit teeth
steps: Offer unlimited hay and monitor chewing, drooling and weight.
Arrange veterinary checks if food drops from the mouth or eating becomes selective.
caution: Dental disease cannot be safely assessed or treated at home.

title: Vaccinations for pet rabbits
steps: Ask a rabbit-savvy vet about current protection against myxomatosis and rabbit haemorrhagic disease.
Keep vaccination records and follow the vet's booster schedule.
caution: Vaccine recommendations and products vary; consult your vet.

title: Neutering discussions
steps: Discuss neutering benefits, risks and timing with an experienced vet.
Plan recovery space and follow post-operative instructions.
caution: Do not fast rabbits before surgery unless your vet gives specific instructions.

title: Parasites and itchy skin
steps: Check for unusual scratching, flakes, hair loss or ear discomfort.
Arrange a vet appointment for diagnosis and suitable treatment.
caution: Never use dog or cat flea treatments on rabbits without veterinary approval.

title: Signs of pain
steps: Watch for hiding, hunched posture, reluctance to move and loud tooth grinding.
Note when symptoms started and seek veterinary help.
caution: Rabbits often conceal illness; do not wait for dramatic symptoms.

title: Breathing concerns
steps: Watch for nasal discharge, noisy breathing or increased effort.
Keep the rabbit calm and contact a vet promptly.
caution: Open-mouth breathing or severe distress requires emergency care.

title: Flystrike prevention
steps: Check the rear end at least daily and more often in warm weather.
Keep accommodation clean and ask your vet about suitable prevention.
caution: Any eggs or maggots on a rabbit require immediate emergency veterinary treatment.

title: Monitoring body condition
steps: Weigh your rabbit regularly using the same safe method.
Track trends and discuss unexpected changes with your vet.
caution: Weight loss can be an early sign of dental or other disease.

title: Emergency transport planning
steps: Keep a secure carrier lined with a towel ready.
Save the emergency vet's number and prepare a concise symptom history.
caution: Do not delay transport while trying unverified home treatments.

title: Baby rabbits and weaning
steps: Ask a rabbit-savvy vet or rescue for age-specific diet and housing advice.
Introduce handling gently and monitor growth and droppings.
caution: Young rabbits have sensitive digestion; avoid sudden food changes.

title: Senior rabbit comfort
steps: Provide low-entry litter trays, non-slip flooring and accessible hay and water.
Arrange regular vet reviews for mobility, teeth and body condition.
caution: Reduced movement or appetite should not be dismissed as old age.

title: Supporting rabbits with mobility problems
steps: Put food, water and resting areas close together.
Use soft flooring and ask a vet about pain management and hygiene.
caution: Never give human painkillers to rabbits.

title: Fireworks and loud noise
steps: Provide a secure, quiet hiding area and keep the normal routine.
Close curtains where appropriate and check the enclosure is secure.
caution: Avoid forcing frightened rabbits out of hiding.

title: Travelling safely with rabbits
steps: Use a well-ventilated secure carrier with a non-slip base and hay.
Keep journeys calm and avoid excessive heat or cold.
caution: Seek veterinary advice for long journeys or rabbits with health problems.

title: Holiday care arrangements
steps: Choose a rabbit-experienced sitter who knows feeding and emergency signs.
Leave written routines, vet contacts and medication instructions.
caution: A rabbit refusing food needs immediate action, not a wait-and-see approach.
